name: The Finite Element Method for Fluid-Structure Interaction with Open-Source Software
description:
- Motivation and presentation of surface-coupled phenomena in nature and engineering
- Governing equations for structures, fluid flows, and their coupling
- Continuum mechanical fundamentals for the analysis of problems on moving meshes (ALE-description)
- Space and time discretization of the governing equations: main concepts, problems, and remedies
- Numerical solution of structure and fluid equations with finite elements: element formulations, boundary conditions, implementation, and solution aspects
- Geometrical description of coupling interface and its identification for complex problems: "embedded" and "body-fitted" approaches
- Formulation of the discretized coupled problem; derivation and discussion of different solution strategies
- Selected advanced topics in FEM-based modeling and simulation of FSI: flows about rotating components, meshing strategies, free-surface flows, particle methods, ...
- Overview of Software-strategies and implementation aspects for FEM-based multiphysics-simulation
- Introduction to FEM-simulation of fluid-structure interaction problems with open-source software Kratos
- Elaboration of own exercises using Python
prerequisites: Sound knowledge in mathematics and numerical methods as well as in mechanics, structural analysis, fluid mechanics, and finite element methods
